transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton.
House Republicans quashed an effort tonight to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth
in a near party-line vote.
President Trump has stood by Hegseth, but many Republicans blamed the Iran war for their
election losses.
NPR's Tom Bowman says the vote comes after Hegseth delivered a defiant defense to the
Articles of Impeachment filed by outgoing Kentucky Republican Congressman Thomas Massey.
He said all these military missions were lawful, and he noted that past presidents were never
called to task for their own operations at some question whether they violated the War
Powers Act.
Most of these impeachment articles have to do with the wars in Iran and Yemen.
By the way, he called Congressman Thomas Massey a "disgruntled, defeated congressman" in
talk of impeachment as far as a show trial.
NPR's Tom Bowman reporting.
The Republican-led House Oversight Committee says the Trump administration mishandled the
release of records related to Jeffrey Epstein in a new report.
The committee faults the Trump administration for missing deadlines and failing to protect
victims' identities.
The report comes nearly a year after Congress required the release of the documents.
Democrats have used the issue to accuse Republicans of protecting the wealthy.
The political power shift in Congress could have big implications for air travel.
NPR's Joel Rose reports the travel industry is bracing for the possibility of another
government shutdown.
U.S. air travelers suffered through three partial government shutdowns over the past
two years, with Republicans in charge of the White House and Congress.
Jeff Freeman, the head of the U.S. Travel Association, says it is hard to predict what
will happen when Democrats take control of the House and Senate next year.
The unpredictability certainly has us in the mindset of buckle up.
In past shutdowns, TSA officers and air traffic controllers sometimes did not get paid.
Many eventually called out sick and took on second jobs to pay their bills, leading to
hours-long security lines, as well as delayed and canceled flights.
Freeman says a divided government makes another shutdown more likely.
Joel Rose, NPR News, Washington.
Pennsylvania has reported more than 1,500 measles cases so far this year and six related
deaths.
The hardest hit area is Lancaster County, the heart of Amish country, as NPR's Maria
Godoy reports.
Surveys suggest only about a third of Amish families in Lancaster County vaccinate their
children, often for cultural and practical rather than religious reasons.
But as measles spreads, health officials have been building trust by vaccinating Amish people
in their homes and hosting frequent vaccine clinics advertised solely by word of mouth.
Dr. Jennifer Wallace is with the Pennsylvania Department of Health.
They tend to be a community that does not want to have a lot of big hoopla, but also
the choice to vaccinate they consider to be a very private one.
She says the state will keep on offering these low-key vaccinations for as long as people
want them.
Maria Godoy, NPR News.
This is NPR.
The FDA is adding a new warning about possible rare cases of vision loss reported with popular
drugs used for GLP-1 weight loss and diabetes, like Ozimpic.
The new language warns doctors of a rare eye condition that can cause loss of vision in
one eye.
The agency says the problem can be permanent and is not fully understood, and it occurs
only in a tiny fraction of patients.
Peggy Rothman, the author and illustrator behind kids' books, classics like Goodnight
Gorilla and Officer Buckle and Gloria, has died.
She was 73 years old, as NPR's Andrew Limbong reports her new books.
Her books have sold millions of copies.
In Goodnight Gorilla, a zookeeper goes around saying goodnight to all the animals while
a wily gorilla sneaks behind him and slowly unlocks each cage.
The book is silly and fun, and you feel like you're in on the mischief with the gorilla.
Peggy Rothman was born in St. Paul, Minnesota before studying children's book writing and
illustration in Los Angeles.
In 1996, she won a Caldecott for her book, Officer Buckle and Gloria, about a police
officer at an assembly for kids being upstaged by his dog, Gloria.
Jen Loja, president of Penguin Young Readers, said in a statement, "We are fortunate that
her stories will continue to delight children and families for generations to come."
Andrew Limbong, NPR News.
Billy Idol, Oasis Wu-Tang Clan, Phil Collins, Chardet, Iron Maiden, Queen Latifah, Joy Division,
New Order, and the late Luther Vandross are set to be inducted into the Rock and Roll
Hall of Fame on Saturday.
The ceremony will take place at the Peacock Theatre in Los Angeles.
This is NPR News from Washington.

topics.text: House Republicans defeat effort to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth over Iran and Yemen wars
House Oversight Committee report faults Trump administration over mishandled Jeffrey Epstein records release
Travel industry braces for possible government shutdown after Congress power shift next year
Pennsylvania reports over 1,500 measles cases and six deaths, hardest hit in Lancaster County
FDA adds warning about rare vision loss cases tied to GLP-1 weight loss and diabetes drugs
Children's author and illustrator Peggy Rothman, of Goodnight Gorilla, dies at 73
Billy Idol, Oasis, Wu-Tang Clan and others set for Rock and Roll Hall of Fame induction Saturday
